• Use indirect authority to hold program owners accountable for comprehensive plans aligned to the strategy and for execution that follows through
• Establish review cadences, effective and efficient communication structures, and governance that keep teams aligned without becoming a bottleneck
• Build a culture of shared ownership, honest measurement, and continuous improvement
 Measure and Optimize

• Work with Marketing Operations to build measurement models and dashboards that connect campaigns to pipeline, revenue, and other identified core KPIs
• Regularly report to leadership on campaign performance, give channel owners a stage to share insights, and demonstrate how the framework is improving marketing effectiveness
• Apply real-time learnings to in-campaign optimizations across channels, and evaluate post-campaign learnings to inform future strategy, amplify what is working, and help the team stop what isn’t working quickly

title: Mid Market Account Manager - Abu Dhabi
description:
Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 Why Deliveroo 
 Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops, and riders. We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.
 We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, and looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas. 
 The team 
 As Deliveroo continues to scale, we become a major revenue channel for restaurants - aside from providing best-in-class support, we are restaurant consultants that use data-driven insight and industry knowledge to help our partner restaurants grow. Our account management team owns and manages restaurant relationships. We are restaurant consultants who use data-driven analytics and industry knowledge to provide best-in-class support and strategic value to our restaurant partners. The Account Managers are a passionate, dynamic group of team players who work well together and cross-functionally with other departments, and of course, they’re fun, personable, and great at building exceptional relationships.
 Role overview 
 As a Mid Market Account Manager, you will manage a portfolio of restaurant partners on Deliveroo, with a focus on high-performing Local Gems and selected national chains. These partners play an important role in attracting customers to the marketplace and represent strong growth opportunities for Deliveroo.
 You will work closely with your partners to improve operational performance, drive marketing initiatives, and identify opportunities to grow their business on the Deliveroo platform. You will also collaborate with internal teams across marketing, operations, and commercial functions to ensure partners deliver a strong customer experience while achieving sustainable growth.
 What will you be doing 
• Manage a portfolio of mid-market restaurant partners, acting as their main point of contact at Deliveroo
• Build strong relationships with partners and run regular performance and business reviews
• Identify and execute growth opportunities to increase order volume and partner performance
• Monitor operational metrics and support partners in improving service quality
• Drive adoption of Deliveroo marketing tools, promotions, and campaigns
• Support partner onboarding and expansion onto the Deliveroo platform
• Collaborate with internal teams to resolve issues and drive partner success
 What skills you need 
• 3+ years in a commercial role in a fast-paced environment
• Strong relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills
• Commercial mindset with the ability to identify growth opportunities
• Analytical ability to interpret performance data and drive actions
• Clear communication and influencing skills with partners and internal teams
• Strong organisation and ability to manage multiple accounts
• Problem-solving mindset and ability to navigate operational challenges
• Collaborative approach when working cross-functionally
• Fluency in Arabic is a plus
• Be based in or willing to relocate to Abu Dhabi 
 Why Join Us? 
 At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. 
 We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders, and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here, you can expect to: 
 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale 
 Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.
🌱 See your impact, fast 
 Ship, test, and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership
 environment.
 🧠Grow through challenge and ownership 
 Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.
 🌎A culture built for builders 
 High standards, collaboration, flexible working, and continuous learning.
 We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find out more about how we hire here . 
 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 
At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.
 We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.
 If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.
 If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!

title: EMEA Statutory Reporting Senior Manager
description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions


ABOUT THE ROLE

Applied Intuition is scaling quickly across entities and geographies, and statutory reporting, clean audits, and compliant local filings are essential. In this London-based role, you will be the accountable owner of statutory reporting, audit, and compliance for our EMEA entities, including the UK, Germany, Sweden, and Saudi Arabia, with more to come.

Reporting to the Director of Accounting, you will lead the EMEA local close and statutory audits, own the filing calendar, oversee the US GAAP to local GAAP conversion work produced by our India-based outsourced accounting team, and partner with Tax, Legal, and Business Technology to automate statutory and compliance processes in NetSuite. This is a hands-on opportunity to build a best-in-class statutory and compliance function across EMEA for a high-growth company.




AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Own the preparation, review, and sign-off of statutory financial statements for our EMEA entities under local GAAP (UK GAAP/FRS 102, German HGB, Swedish K2/K3, and IFRS as endorsed in Saudi Arabia), including the US GAAP to local GAAP conversion and bridge work papers.

 - Lead each statutory audit end to end with our external auditors, from planning and PBC lists through audit queries, adjustments, and management representation letters, closing audits on schedule.

 - Run the EMEA month-end on the US close calendar: review and sign off statutory balance sheet reconciliations, drive aged reconciling items to zero, and maintain local GAAP schedules such as leases and accrued vacation.

 - Own the EMEA statutory and compliance filing calendar, covering VAT, corporate income tax and zakat (with Tax and external advisers), company registry filings, and annual accounts, so every filing goes in on time with no notices from authorities.

 - Manage the quality and performance of our India-based outsourced accounting team and of in-country auditors, tax advisers, and accounting providers, and turn statutory and conversion workpapers into standard templates the team can run with minimal rework.

 - Partner with Business Technology to automate statutory reporting, VAT, and e-invoicing in NetSuite, design and document the related controls, and bring new entities and regulatory changes (for example, FRS 102 amendments and German and Saudi e-invoicing mandates) into the process ahead of effective dates.




WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, or CPA) with 14+ years of relevant accounting experience

 - Proven ownership of multi-entity UK statutory reporting under UK GAAP (FRS 102) and the Companies Act 2006, including leading statutory audits end to end

 - Experience converting US GAAP to local GAAP and reviewing GAAP bridge workpapers (for example, leases and accrued vacation)

 - Experience managing outsourced or offshore accounting teams, including setting quality standards and reviewing output across time zones

 - Proficiency with NetSuite, ideally in a multi-subsidiary environment

 - Sound judgment on materiality and filing risk, and clear communication with auditors, advisers, and partners across EMEA, the US, and India


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Big 4 or top-tier public accounting background, and in-house experience at a software/technology multinational

 - Hands-on German GAAP (HGB) and GmbH statutory experience

 - Exposure to Swedish (K2/K3) or Saudi (IFRS, zakat, ZATCA e-invoicing) statutory reporting, or other EMEA local GAAPs and languages

 - Working knowledge of VAT, Making Tax Digital, and e-invoicing requirements across EMEA

 - Experience designing internal controls (SOX or audit readiness) and testing finance system automation, including applying AI tools to accounting workflows
   
   

Compensation at Applied Intuition for eligible roles includes base salary, equity, and benefits. Base salary is a single component of the total compensation package, which may also include equity in the form of options and/or restricted stock units, comprehensive health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance coverage, 401k retirement benefits with employer match, learning and wellness stipends, and paid time off. Note that benefits are subject to change and may vary based on jurisdiction of employment.

Applied Intuition pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum intended target base salary for new hire salaries for the position. The actual base salary offered to a successful candidate will additionally be influenced by a variety of factors including experience, credentials & certifications, educational attainment, skill level requirement

 - Cross-Functional Coordination: Work closely with the ecosystem - inside sales, solution architecture, marketing, product, and customer success teams to ensure cohesive go-to-market execution.

title: Engagement Manager - Enterprise Corporates
description:
ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The way legal work gets done is changing, and Engagement is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an Engagement Manager to join our UK & Ireland Engagement team in London, own adoption across a portfolio of enterprise corporate clients and help some of the world's largest in-house legal functions fundamentally change the way they work.

This is a role for someone who has led change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed. You will own the adoption and long-term success of strategic enterprise accounts: building deep, multi-level relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser who turns Legora into an embedded part of how those teams operate.

Enterprise means depth: larger, more complex accounts with more revenue at stake. Each account is a global legal function with multiple teams, jurisdictions and business units, its own governance, and a long, multi-phase roadmap. Success depends on navigating that complexity: aligning General Counsel, legal operations, IT, security and procurement, and building momentum one team and one use case at a time until Legora is used across the whole function.

At the heart of the role is designing each client's enterprise adoption strategy and delivering the change programmes that transform how they work. For every account you will build a tailored, multi-year roadmap, sequence initiatives from the first pilot teams to function-wide and global adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI with executive sponsors, and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class enterprise adoption programme at Legora, helping clients realise measurable ROI, expand successful use cases and transform the way their teams work.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

You'll lead the post-sale customer experience, owning onboarding, adoption and long-term value realisation for a portfolio of enterprise accounts. Specifically, you will:

 - Design each client's enterprise adoption strategy: the change-management approach, governance model, stakeholder map across legal, business and IT, and target outcomes for how that legal function adopts Legora.

 - Execute against that strategy, sequencing initiatives from the first pilot teams through to function-wide and global adoption across regions, practice areas and business units.

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

WorkFusion, a UiPath company, builds AI agents that take on the heavy lifting of financial crime operations. Banks and financial institutions use them to move faster, stay compliant, and scale without adding headcount.

You’ll run discovery workshops, design solutions, build and deliver demos, lead proof-of-value engagements and own content creation across several strategic accounts.

The role sits where Sales meets Product. You’ll bring field intelligence back to the team, influence the roadmap and help shape how WorkFusion goes to market in EMEA. The scope is broad because the bar is high: you move without being asked, figure things out quickly, and connect technical depth to commercial outcomes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO AT UIPATH

Deal Execution

 - Own the solution side of the sales cycle, from qualification through close and expansion

 - Build and deliver tailored demos and proof-of-concept engagements that make the value concrete

 - Lead discovery workshops to uncover real requirements, then turn them into solution designs and WorkFusion business cases

 - Work across multiple AEs and strategic accounts without losing depth or precision

Internal Impact

title: Strategy Lead, Sustainable Delivery
description:
Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 About the Role
 Location: Any Wolt or Deliveroo hub
 The Sustainability & Community Impact team at DoorDash works across our global brands (DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo) to advance the company's approach to the issues that matter most to our business, our communities, and the world we operate in. We sit within the Public Policy function and work closely with other teams on a daily basis.
 We're hiring a Strategy Lead, Sustainable Delivery to help shape our global approach to sustainable delivery and lead its execution. You’ll focus on initiatives that address the environmental impact of our platform and industry, such as alternative vehicles for couriers and sustainable packaging. You’ll dive into the details to understand our biggest opportunities and build programs to scale that meet the needs of couriers, local businesses, and customers. 
 You'll have visibility across a global company, real ownership from day one, and room to build and scale programs that make a difference
 What you'll be doing 
• Co-lead the global sustainable delivery strategy, setting priorities, ambition, and metrics for our work, and be accountable for it globally
• Own key programs in the implementation of that strategy. This will include designing, building, operating, and scaling initiatives across regions, from early pilots through to scaled programs, including partnerships with cities and providers
• Support local sustainability initiatives across markets by giving teams a shared framework, tools, and strategic guidance, so local efforts ladder up to the global strategy
• Use data to prove the biggest opportunities, test ideas through experimentation, and measure and report on program progress.
• Build strong relationships across Operations, Product, Merchant, Market, Policy, and Communications teams to drive strategic sustainability initiatives
 What You’ll Need to Thrive 
 Essential 
• At least five years of experience building and managing complex, operational, and cross-functional programs, including starting things from scratch, ideally in logistics, mobility, retail, or consumer tech
• Data-driven and analytical mindset, with demonstrated experience using data, analytics tools, or SQL to guide decisions and measure defensible impact.
• Knowledge of the environmental sector, including the policy and technology landscape for vehicle electrification, packaging, and circularity
• An operator mindset: you turn high-level goals into actionable plans and enjoy getting into the detail. You make decisions with it and are at ease with measurement tools. 
• A strong cross-functional influencer and excellent communicator, who can align stakeholders while functioning as an individual contributor
• Ease working as a co-lead with a US-based counterpart across time zones, and across several global markets
• A principled, pragmatic view of sustainability: you focus on impact that is real, measurable, and defensible
 Nice to Have 
• Direct experience with e-mobility, fleet electrification, or city and OEM commercial partnerships.
• Experience with sustainable packaging, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), or reuse programs.
 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 
At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.
 We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.
 If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.
 If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!

title: Drones Operations Manager

Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 About the Team
 DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying autonomous aviation technologies in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
 About the Role
 As the Drone Operations Manager for UK & Ireland, you are a player-coach who will stand up our drone delivery operation in the region from nothing. You will personally fly on a regular basis, as a working pilot, while you build the team, find and fit out the operating sites, and help take us through UK CAA and/or Irish Aviation Authority (IAA)/EASA authorisation. You will contribute to the manuals you fly under.
 As we build out the team in 2027, the future Chief Pilot (or equivalent nominated post-holder) and Head of Maintenance will report to you. You will work day to day with engineering and product, in person, at the launch site. This role is on-site and cannot be done remotely.
 What You'll Do Day to Day
 Fly and Operate (a regular part of the job, not occasional): 
• Fly as a pilot in command on a regular rota: aircraft acceptance and commissioning flights, proving flights for the regulator, and live delivery operations.
• Run pre-flight and post-flight checks, site and airspace checks, weather go/no-go decisions, battery and payload handling, and flight logging in line with the Operations Manual.
• Act as visual observer, payload operator or flight supervisor as needed, and be on the ground at launch and landing sites during operations.
• Keep your own pilot competency, currency, recurrent training and flight records up to date, to the standard you set for the team.
• Lead incident, accident and occurrence response in the field and file regulator reports (CAA mandatory occurrence reporting / IAA-EASA equivalent) and run the follow-up investigation.
 Build the Team: 
• Recruit, hire and onboard the first pilots, ops technicians, visual observers, maintenance staff and the nominated safety/compliance post-holders.
• Write the training syllabus and run initial and recurrent training, including practical flight checks, competency assessments, emergency drills and currency tracking.
• Build the duty roster, flight-time and fatigue limits, and on-call coverage.
 Find and Build the Sites: 
• Scout and secure launch/landing sites, hubs and maintenance space near merchant partners. Walk the sites, survey obstacles, flight paths, ground risk and operational suitability, and negotiate access, leases and landowner permissions.
• Oversee on-site fit-out: workshop space, battery charging and storage (including fire protection and lithium battery storage rules), power and connectivity, security, landing pads, signage, first aid and fire equipment.
• Support planning consent and local authority approvals. Own risk assessments, health and safety procedures, and set up all site requirements with support from corporate teams as needed.
• Own the launch plan, budget, vendors and timeline for each site. 
• Lead local community and stakeholder engagement for each site (neighbours, local authorities), including noise and privacy concerns.
• Work with the aircraft provider and engineering on site layout, charging, battery swap and loading equipment.
 Regulatory Authorisation and Compliance: 
• Run the Safety Management System (SMS): hazard reporting, risk assessments, safety reviews, audits and corrective actions.
• Stay compliant with UK GDPR/EU GDPR (ICO or Data Protection Commission), insurance (Regulation 785/2004 and UK equivalent), noise, and local environmental requirements.
• Be the day-to-day contact for the CAA, IAA and air navigation service providers, including audits, inspections and flight demonstrations.
 Scale the Operation: 
• Track flight, delivery and reliability metrics and use them to improve procedures, rotas and site layouts.
• Work with the commercial operations lead to match merchant demand to flight capacity.
• Work with the US drone operations team to adapt proven processes to the UK/Ireland regulatory environment.
 Why You'll Love This Role
• Keep flying: you will be hands-on with aircraft every week while you lead.
• Be at the forefront of autonomous aviation and shape last-mile drone delivery in the EMEA.
• Build a team, a site and an operation from the ground up with autonomy and trust.
• Work directly with engineers who build the aircraft and software you operate.
 What We're Looking For
• Current remote pilot qualifications and significant hands-on UAS flight experience (including BVLOS or complex operations), with a CAA or EASA-recognised pilot competency (e.g. A2 CofC, GVC/OSC-level, or national equivalent).
• Experience holding or managing UK CAA Operational Authorisations and/or EASA Specific category authorisations (or LUC).
• Proven ability to write and enforce SOPs, checklists and Operations Manuals.
• Working knowledge of UK CAA / IAA / EASA regulations, SORA, airspace and compliance frameworks.
• Experience leading and training pilots, and starting up or scaling flight operations.
• Practical experience setting up an operating site: finding space, working with landlords, contractors and local authorities, and handling battery storage and site safety.
• Background in risk assessment, SMS, and emergency response.
• Willingness to work in the field in all weather, including early mornings, evenings and weekends, as operations require.
 Bonus Qualifications

title: Product Operations Manager
description:
We’re Capital on Tap 👋
 💳 Capital on Tap started because small businesses were underserved. Big banks were slow, their products weren't fit for purpose, and small business owners often couldn't access what they needed. We set out to fix that. 
 Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. We offer a best-in-class business credit card, SME-focused spend management platform, a savings product that hit £1 billion in funds within its first year, and a growing suite of tools and financial products that make running a small business easier. 
 1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We’ve done a pretty good job so far, but we’re just getting started! 
 Product at Capital on Tap 
 Our Product team sits at the heart of everything we build. We move fast, work closely with engineering, and obsess over outcomes for our customers. Product Operations makes sure what we launch works as intended, for our customers and for the teams that run it. 
 The Role 
 We are looking for a Product Operations Manager to join our growing Product Operations team. You will own the day-to-day operational health of your product area - Cards, from launch readiness through to post-launch performance. You will work closely with Engineering, Compliance, Customer Operations and external partners to drive new initiatives and improvements, so that our customers get the best possible account. 
 You will be a trusted operator across multiple workstreams: independently leading large projects, mentoring more junior team members, and starting to shape Product Operations processes and ways of working. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
• Owning the operational strategy and performance of the cards domain, setting KPIs and targets, and being accountable for quality, output and commercial impact 
• Owning the rollout of a new products and features end to end, from planning through to a stable, bug-free release 
• Monitoring and analysing product performance data (approval rates, acceptance rates, failure rates, SLA metrics) to identify issues and inform optimisation 
• Lead improvements to our authorisation and authentication performance, resolving merchant acceptance and clearing issues so our card is accepted globally 
• Support global card programme management in partnership with scheme partners (Visa), including global stock management. 
• Owning relationships with key partners, internal and external, including scheme partners and vendors, and being trusted by the senior management team to do so 
• Generating your own strategic ideas for pilots and workstreams, and influencing the right stakeholders to back them and get them live 
 What We're Looking For 
• 5+ years of experience in product operations, payments operations or a similar role, including managing a small team 
• Subject matter expertise in a product area, and a close working relationship with the Product Manager for that area 
• Sound judgement: you are trusted to make your own calls in your area without needing approval, with good instincts for what is right 
• A track record of near-independent product and feature rollouts and autonomous pilots, with results reported to senior management 
• Deep card payments and card scheme knowledge in the debit or credit card industry, with working experience of Visa or Mastercard scheme rules 
• Experience working with Risk, Credit, Compliance and Legal to get projects over the line, and accountability for meeting regulatory, risk and compliance requirements 
• Clear writing and speaking, tailored for audiences from Sales and Engineering to Customer Service and QA 
• The ability to frame a case to influence decision makers, manage up effectively and build relationships at all seniority levels 
• Excellent stakeholder, vendor and commercial management skills 
• Intermediate SQL and Looker skills 
 Our Hiring Bar 
 Alongside the role-specific experience above, every Product Operations candidate is assessed against a shared set of traits that we look for regardless of level or product area. 
• Deals with ambiguity: Doesn't need a fully formed brief to start moving. Handles priorities or requirements shifting mid-flight without getting stuck. 
• Data-driven decision making: Uses operational, customer, and performance data to inform decisions, balance short- and long-term trade-offs, and quantify impact on revenue, retention, cost, and risk.

title: Customer Relations Leader
description:
CUSTOMER RELATIONS LEADER

Full-time, 40 hours a week + a comprehensive benefits package | London office, 5 days a week | Starting as soon as possible

Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services have made life harder for them, with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that. We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe, bringing together payments, business accounts and other business tools with simple technology and real human support. From card payments and business accounts to financing solutions, we help our Members spend less time worrying about their finances and more time doing what they love.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you’re a natural leader who cares about people and wants to make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Mission

Every Member who reaches us is a small business owner trying to keep their doors open. We treat every interaction like welcoming a guest, not processing a ticket. We call it heartwarming hospitality.

As a Customer Relations Leader, you set the tone for what that looks like day to day. You’ll lead a pod of up to 10 Customer Relations Agents within our wider Customer Relations team, reporting to the Head of Customer Management. You’re the first line of support for your team, and you’re accountable for the quality, consistency and warmth of the service they deliver. You’ll coach your team to bring genuine care into every call, email and chat, while holding the bar on getting the actual problem solved.

This is a role for someone who models heartwarming hospitality themselves and builds a team that does the same, consistently and under pressure.

Your responsibilities will include:

 - Lead your pod: Coach and develop a team of up to 10 Customer Relations Agents through regular 1-1s, call and chat listening, and real-time feedback.

 - Set the standard: Model heartwarming hospitality and hold your agents accountable to it in every interaction.

 - Own performance: Manage day-to-day performance against quality, productivity and Member satisfaction targets.

 - Handle escalations: Be the escalation point for complex or sensitive Member cases your team can’t resolve alone.

 - Develop your team: Run onboarding, training and ongoing skill development, including for agents who are new to the industry.

 - Keep things running: Manage scheduling, attendance and workload across your pod, so coverage stays consistent.

 - Spot the patterns: Identify recurring themes and friction points, and feed them back to the Head of Customer Relations and the wider business.

 - Fix root causes: Work with Product, Supply Chain, Customer Due Diligence and Sales to tackle the issues behind avoidable Member contact.

 - Report and plan: Report on your team’s KPIs and contribute to wider Customer Relations planning.

Your Story

We believe great leaders come from all kinds of backgrounds.

You might be leading a team in a contact centre today. Or you might have led a team in hospitality, where making every guest feel welcome is simply part of the job.

What matters most to us is how you lead people, the standards you hold and how you bring out the best in your team.

We’re looking for people who bring:

 - Proven leadership: Clear ownership of a team’s performance and quality, and evidence of how you’ve improved both.

 - A coaching track record: You’ve helped people improve their numbers and how they show up for customers.

 - Warmth and empathy: You’re a naturally warm leader who models the standard you expect from your team.

 - Composure under pressure: You stay calm and constructive, especially when supporting your team through a difficult or emotional case.

 - Sound judgement: Strong commercial awareness, and you know when to escalate and when to make the call yourself.

 - Confidence with data: You use performance data to drive coaching, not just to report on it.

 - Strong presence: You hold your own and raise issues constructively, upwards as well as downwards.

 - Excellent communication: You communicate clearly with your team and with colleagues across the business.

You’ll also need:

 - At least one year’s experience leading a team in a contact centre or hospitality environment.

 - Fluency in English, spoken and written.

 - The right to work in the UK.

 - The ability to work 40 hours a week from our London office, five days a week.

The Perks

We believe great work should be recognised and rewarded. Alongside the opportunity to build your career in a growing European fintech, you’ll receive:

 - The chance to shape a growing team and how we look after our Members.

 - Ongoing support and development to grow as a leader at Teya.

 - 25 days of paid annual leave, plus UK bank holidays.

 - Bupa private healthcare and life insurance.

 - Employer pension contributions through our company pension scheme.

 - Free gym membership through Wellhub, alongside one-to-one therapy sessions, meditation and digital fitness and nutrition apps.

 - Enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

 - Cycle-to-Work Scheme.

 - Office snacks every day, in a friendly, comfortable office in Central London.

title: Delivery Manager
description:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.



We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.



Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.



AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

 
 


ABOUT THE TEAM 

 

Our Public Services Business Unit is committed to leveraging AI for the benefit of individual citizens and the public good.

From our work informing strategic government decisions, to optimising our NHS, through to reducing bureaucratic backlogs - we know that AI offers opportunities to drive improvements at every level of Government and we are proud to lead on some of the most impactful work happening in the sector.

Because of the nature of the work we do with our Government clients, you may need to be eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC) and willing to work on site with these clients from time to time.

 
 


ABOUT THE ROLE

 

As a Delivery Manager in our Public Services team at Faculty, you will act as a pivotal commercial and delivery lead, driving high-stakes AI transformation for the UK’s most critical government partners.

You will be a key point of contact for both our external clients and internal technical teams, building deep networks of influence and solving complex challenges by bridging the gap between cutting-edge AI research and operational mission needs.

With an entrepreneurial spirit, you will work with multidisciplinary teams to ensure every project delivers meaningful, long-term value in a fast-evolving landscape.






WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

 

 - Owning the end-to-end delivery of our AI projects for prominent clients across the Public Services space

title: Principal Product Manager II, AI/Vectors  Elasticsearch
description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.
 What is The Role 
 We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead the strategy and roadmap for Elastic's embedding/reranking and vector database and related capabilities. In this senior role, you'll be the go-to expert on search/vector search, guiding the direction for technologies like vector indexing and hybrid retrieval. This position offers the chance to shape a vital part of our product, working closely with engineering and research teams to ensure that our offerings meet the needs of numerous organizations while keeping pace with the evolving landscape of AI. 
 What You Will Be Doing 
• 
 Conduct market research to uncover emerging trends in search/vector databases as well as SOTA model research in emerging areas to manage unstructured data, working alongside our model team. 
• 
 Evaluate the competitive landscape to enhance product positioning and develop user personas that guide feature decisions. 
• 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align the product strategy with business goals while prioritizing features based on customer feedback and market demands. 
• 
 Establish long-term product goals and milestones for the vector use cases, document AI and unstructured data management to drive its development. Prioritize features and enhancements based on user feedback and technical feasibility. Allocate resources skillfully to ensure timely updates, while coordinating with engineering teams to validate roadmap assumptions. Communicate updates and expectations clearly to stakeholders and executives. 
• 
 Own the vision, strategy, and multi-quarter roadmap for Elastic's vector database as well as core search use cases, from low-level indexing internals to the developer-facing APIs and SDKs. 
• 
 Partner deeply with engineering and applied research on trade-offs, be a credible technical peer in those conversations. Define and defend the metrics that matter: recall, latency, index size, ingestion throughput, and total cost of ownership. Advance the competitiveness of Elastic AI and Vector products across all deployments - Serverless and Self-managed. 
• 
 Define a unified strategy and roadmap across embedding/reranking models and vector indexing/ semantic ingestion, model lifecycle, and end-to-end retrieval quality. 
• 
 Manage the operating cadence. Make sure shared metrics and priorities align the research, cloud, and engineering teams. Address trade-offs where model and index decisions intersect. 
 What You Bring 
• 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field 
• 
 Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred 
• 
 8+ years in product management, with significant time on technical infrastructure, databases, search, or ML/AI platforms. 
• 
 You should have good working knowledge of vector search fundamentals. This includes embeddings, ANN indexing, similarity metrics, and trade-offs between recall and latency. Additionally, you need to know about hybrid retrieval. 
• 
 You should have a working knowledge of generative models, model fine tuning, model capabilities and document processing for large corpus 
• 
 You don't need to be a researcher, but you should hold your own with engineers on these topics. A track record of shipping developer- or infrastructure-facing products that were adopted at scale.

Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. title: Principal GTM Operations Analyst
description:
GTM Operations & Strategy at MongoDB is a global team of builders and innovators focused on unleashing MongoDB’s sales greatness by pairing world‑class analytics with scalable operations. Within GTM Operations, the GTM Intelligence - Applied Science team turns complex GTM data into tools, models, and insights that help our sales organization make better, faster decisions across our people, segmentation, territory design, forecasting, and account prioritization.
 As a Principal Analyst on the Applied Science team, you will set the technical direction for our GTM model portfolio and personally lead our highest‑stakes programs, from framing problems with SVP‑level stakeholders, through data engineering and model design, to productionalized workflows, dashboards, and executive‑ready narratives that change how the field operates. This role will be based remotely in the United States, and supports a global stakeholder set across regions and GTM functions.
 What You’ll Do
 Own the model portfolio and roadmap for one or more domains
• Set the multi‑quarter roadmap for a given GTM model portfolio domain, deciding what to build, retire, or invest in based on measured business impact
• Act as the senior analytical thought partner to GTM leadership, shaping which questions the team takes on, not just how it answers them
 Translate GTM questions into analytical projects
• Partner with GTM Ops, Sales Strategy & Planning, Sales Leadership, and Central Analytics to scope problems, define success criteria, and prioritize work across areas like segmentation, territory design, account prioritization, and pipeline/forecast health
• Structure ambiguous questions into hypotheses, analytical plans, and clear recommendations for senior stakeholders (SVPs, RVPs, functional leaders)
 Design and build scalable analytics & models
• Develop and maintain statistical and machine learning models (e.g., NARR prediction, deal qualification, account momentum, workload identification) that inform forecast expectations, territory assignments, and deal prioritization
• Engineer robust data pipelines and features (SQL/Python) on top of our GTM data stack (Salesforce, product usage, call transcripts, marketing signals, etc.) in partnership with data and platform teams
 Own core GTM analytics assets
• Lead flagship programs such as Forecasting 3.0 / Atlas Forecasting Calculator, Customer 360 Revamp, GTM Metrics 3.0, and territory optimization initiatives, ensuring they are statistically sound, explainable, and operationally durable
• Build and govern self‑serve analytics assets (e.g., Sigma workbooks, curated datasets) that allow GTM stakeholders to answer their own questions safely and consistently
 Measure and prove impact
• Design experiments, holdouts, and causal analyses that quantify the revenue and efficiency impact of our models and GTM investments, and make that evidence the basis for investment decisions
 Turn analysis into decisions and change
• Deliver concise, executive‑ready narratives (memos, scorecards, and QBR/MBR content) that highlight trade‑offs and explicit recommendations, not just data and charts
• Run stakeholder working sessions to align on scenarios, validate model outcomes, and embed recommendations into operating rhythms (e.g., segmentation reviews, annual planning, forecast calls)
 Advance our GTM data & AI foundations
• Define how we use new GTM data sources such as call transcript modeling, workload inference, and account intelligence to unlock novel scoring and routing use cases
• Set the standards for testing, monitoring, documentation, and change management of GTM models and analytics products, in partnership with Central Analytics and GTM Tech
 Multiply the team
• Mentor analysts and data scientists, review their technical work, and raise the bar for rigor across our teams
• Create clear documentation, playbooks, and training to help other analysts and GTM stakeholders understand and safely use the models, tools, and datasets you own
• Contribute to a strong culture of technical rigor, peer review, and knowledge sharing within Sales Intelligence and the broader GTM Operations community
 What We’re Looking For
 Experience

description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Head of Healthcare to own ElevenLabs' US healthcare business across providers, payers, and life sciences. Health organizations want agents that talk to patients, members, and clinicians and that are safe, fast, and compatible with the systems they already run. You'll own the healthcare business from strategy and pipeline through to the team that delivers the revenue.

We don't use traditional job titles at ElevenLabs. This role is equivalent in scope and seniority to a Vice President of Healthcare, with ownership of the vertical, authority to hire and lead the sales team, and the chance to work closely with ElevenLabs leaders across the company.

Healthcare buyers hold vendors to a high bar on safety, compliance, and reliability, and we're looking for a leader who has met that bar before. You'll build the healthcare business end to end, including the strategy, team, pipeline, and playbook. You'll stay close to the most strategic deals while hiring and developing the leaders who will run segments as the business grows.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Define and execute the healthcare go-to-market strategy across health systems, payers, and life sciences (pharma and medtech).

 - Own the healthcare revenue number, forecast accuracy, pipeline quality, and sales process, working with Revenue Operations on clean data and clear insight.

 - Recruit and lead the sales team, starting with Account Executives and adding segment leaders as the business grows. Coach reps on deal strategy and execution, and develop future leaders.

 - Define the enterprise ICP, sales methodology, and a repeatable motion for each segment.

 - Lead the largest strategic pursuits with your team, and own the executive relationships at our most important health systems, payers, and life sciences companies.

 - Build the customer reference base that establishes ElevenLabs as a trusted partner across healthcare.

 - Build our approach to BAA, security, and AI governance review (including MLR for pharma), and develop the executive relationships with Compliance, Privacy, and IT security leaders that health organizations require.

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering, and Customer Success leaders to shape what we build, integrate, and bring to market for health organizations.

 - Establish how we land and expand with each health organization, from first deployment through enterprise-wide adoption.

 - Define our position against build-vs-buy decisions, platform bundlers, and vertical point solutions.

 - Represent ElevenLabs at industry events and in high-stakes negotiations.

title: Retention & Recovery Lead
description:
Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

The role

The Retention & Recovery Lead owns one pipeline that follows every merchant from the first sign they might leave, through retention, a well-run exit and collections, to write-off or debt sale.

Today we treat churn and collections as separate problems, and neither has a clear owner. In practice they are usually the same merchant at different points in time: a merchant who goes quiet in March becomes, by June, an unpaid fee, a terminal still in the field and a balance nobody is chasing. Collections activity also sits in pockets across the business, from unpaid subscriptions and fees, negative balances and chargebacks to terminal recovery, dissolved companies and fraud losses. As our credit products grow, so will the need.

You’ll bring all of this together under one strategy, one queue and one set of metrics. We want someone who knows collections and its pain points, and who approaches the whole lifecycle with a product and design mindset: redesigning journeys end to end, and deciding where AI and automation belong and where people add the most value. You’ll start hands-on and build a small credit control team as the capability grows.

What you’ll do

 - Own the retention-to-recovery pipeline end to end, from the first churn signal to write-off or debt sale, running from one prioritised queue with one set of definitions.

 - Work with our data team to build and run an AI retention engine that identifies merchants heading towards churn, recommends the next best action for each and puts them in a queue to be worked. Prove what works with holdout groups, and do more of it.

 - Agree with Commercial how save conversations are delivered, and make sure our own risk actions, such as held settlements, are weighed before they push a good merchant out.

 - Design a proper exit for every merchant who leaves: a recorded reason, fees stopped, terminal returned, final balance netted and a final statement, so merchants do not need to contact Customer Relations to close their account.

 - Build automated collections that start the day a balance turns negative: settlement netting, direct debit, card on file, payment links and payment plans. Journeys run through the Teya app and portal first, with phone as the exception.

 - Run managed and external recovery for larger balances: credit control, payment plans, an agency panel, write-off thresholds and, as a last resort, debt sale.

 - Own the recovery strategy for fraud-related balances with Fraud Operations and Legal. They keep investigation and legal action; you make sure every balance has a recovery route and a priority.

 - Run the existing book as a separate remediation project with its own end date, so it does not pull focus from the new flow.

 - Connect the work of Billing, Payments, Logistics (terminal recovery), Credit, Customer Relations and the termination and withheld funds process into one joined-up flow.

 - Define and own the pipeline’s metrics, report them monthly, and feed what you learn back into onboarding, pricing and risk policy.

 - Prepare the capability to scale with Teya’s growing credit book, and hire and lead the credit control team.

What success looks like

In your first six months

 - Definitions agreed and reported for flow recovery rate, stock recovery rate and true churn.

 - A single queue live, worked by hand from simple rules while the model is built.

 - An exit process in place for every leaving merchant, and an automated collections first version running in at least one market.

 - The credit control team hired or in hiring, and the legacy book project under way with a clear plan.

By the end of your first year

 - The first retention model live, beating the rules-based baseline and tested against holdout groups.

 - Flow recovery rate by day 90 tracking towards our 70% target, with time to recovery and cost to collect reported monthly.

 - The first debt sale completed, where the legal and data preconditions are met.

 - Measurably fewer Customer Relations contacts from merchants who are leaving or owe us money.

What you’ll bring

 - Hands-on collections or recovery experience at some point in your career, ideally with small businesses, covering payment plans, agencies and write-offs, so you know where the pain points sit.

 - Experience with retention, churn or customer lifecycle work, or a clear view of how retention and collections connect.

 - A strong product mindset: you think in journeys, systems and outcomes, not only operational volume.

 - A track record of designing, rolling out and running new processes, shipping a working first version quickly and improving it.

 - A practical, curious approach to AI and automation, with the judgement to know where they help and where they don’t.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

Your Mission

We are looking for a Head of Capital and Liquidity Planning to lead Teya’s first-line prudential framework and help ensure that our growth is supported by robust capital, liquidity and risk management.

Reporting to the CFO, you will own the practical delivery of Teya’s prudential agenda across capital adequacy, liquidity adequacy, stress testing, ICAAP, ILAAP and contingency planning. You will work closely with Treasury, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Product and Operations to turn prudential requirements into clear decisions, effective controls and usable management information.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable moving between strategic judgement and detailed analysis. You will help the business understand its prudential position, anticipate emerging risks and make well-informed decisions about growth, funding, products and resilience. You will act as the key liaison between Treasury and FP&A, owning capital and liquidity regulatory calculations within forecasting models and ensuring that prudential considerations are embedded in planning.\



Responsibilities

 - Own and continuously improve Teya’s first-line prudential framework, including capital, liquidity, risk appetite, stress testing and contingency planning.

 - Lead or coordinate the ICAAP, ILAAP, Recovery and Resolution Plan (RRP) and Solvent Wind Down Plan (SWDP), ensuring that each reflects the business model, risk profile, forward plan and realistic management actions.

 - Act as the key liaison between Treasury and FP&A, owning capital and liquidity regulatory and internal EWI / KRI calculations in forecasting models.

 - Run the ICAAP, ILAAP, RRP and SWDP through relevant governance committees, coordinating across Risk, Finance, Product, Commercial, Treasury and Compliance.

 - Produce clear analysis and recommendations for the CFO, senior leadership and relevant governance forums, to facilitate decision making on trade-offs.

 - Establish forward-looking monitoring of capital and liquidity positions, headroom, triggers, concentrations, funding needs and stress outcomes.

 - Work with Product, Commercial, Operations, Finance and Risk on new products, material changes and growth initiatives, ensuring prudential impacts and controls are understood before scale-up.



Requirements

 - 10–15 years of total experience in prudential risk, capital, liquidity, regulatory reporting, Treasury, Finance or a closely related discipline within a regulated financial services environment.

 - 6–8 years of experience contributing to and leading or coordinating one or, ideally, more of bank ICAAP, ILAAP, Recovery and Resolution Plans (RRP) and Solvent Wind Down Plans (SWDP).

 - Expert-level understanding of current and evolving regulatory expectations for capital and liquidity adequacy assessment processes in the UK, and preferably in EU jurisdictions too.

 - Commercial sensitivity and judgement to optimise risk-adjusted returns on capital and liquidity while staying within — and, where needed, influencing — risk appetite and control design.

 - Strong practical knowledge of capital and liquidity adequacy, stress testing, recovery and resolution planning, solvent wind-down planning and contingency actions.

 - Strong analytical skills, with the judgement to identify what matters and communicate it clearly to senior stakeholders.

 - A control-minded approach: you care about data quality, evidence, governance and follow-through, not just the final number.

 - The confidence to challenge constructively, influence senior stakeholders and work effectively across functions.

 - Experience working through periods of major change or bank builds is a plus.

 - The ability to work in a dynamic, technology-driven organisation with multiple product lines, different jurisdictions and evolving governance structures.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Nice to have:

 - Experience in payments, e-money, banking, lending or another technology-enabled regulated financial services business.

 - Experience working with UK and/or European prudential regulators and regulatory submissions.

 - Experience building or enhancing prudential frameworks during periods of significant organisational or regulatory change.
   
   

What this role offers

 - The opportunity to shape a critical first-line capability at a growing financial services business.

 - Direct exposure to the CFO and senior leadership, with the opportunity to influence strategic decisions.

 - A broad remit spanning capital, liquidity, governance and contingency planning.

 - A collaborative, international environment where people are encouraged to take ownership and make things better.

 - A role with visible impact on Teya’s resilience and on the small businesses we serve.



The Perks

title: Principal Revenue Strategist
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
 The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
 * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 An overview of this role 
 As a Principal Revenue Strategist, you'll help shape how GitLab brings its products to market as artificial intelligence changes how software is built and bought. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Strategy, you'll be a senior individual contributor connecting market, product, and field insights to clear recommendations and changes in how we sell. You'll take on complex, open-ended go-to-market questions with limited context, working directly with executive partners across Sales, Finance, and Product to decide where to invest, how to reach customers, and what needs to change.
 What you'll do 
• Shape revenue strategy across customer segmentation, sales coverage, sales motions, and investment priorities.
• Design multi-quarter changes in how we sell and monetize, defining the implications for the customer journey, metrics, roles, incentives, and operating model. Build agreement on the path forward and partner with Field Operations and Enablement on execution.
• Develop market and expansion strategies, prioritizing markets, defining go-to-market models and capacity needs, and identifying the operational dependencies of entering or scaling in new regions.
• Connect go-to-market strategy and Product by translating field and customer insights into product input, and product direction into commercial implications. Provide focused, commercially grounded input on pricing and packaging.
• Contribute strategic inputs to long-range planning, including total addressable market, sales capacity, productivity, and unit economics, while Field Operations and Finance retain ownership of annual planning, quota setting, and territory design.
• Build models, write decision memos, run analyses, and facilitate working sessions to turn recommendations into action with cross-functional partners.
• Advise senior leaders in Sales, Finance, and Product independently, distilling complex problems into clear recommendations with explicit assumptions and trade-offs.
 What you'll bring 
• Experience owning complex go-to-market or revenue strategy work in a growing technology company, consulting, or a combination of both. Relevant experience and transferable skills matter more than a particular career path.
• Direct experience solving business-to-business software go-to-market problems, such as segmentation, coverage, pipeline and conversion, sales capacity and productivity, incentives, or pricing and packaging.
• A structured approach to testing assumptions and turning an unclear problem into a framework, a recommendation, and practical next steps.
• Strong commercial and analytical judgment, including the ability to build models and recognize when the evidence is sufficient to make a decision.
• The ability to work credibly with senior leaders, challenge decisions with evidence, and influence people without formal authority.
• A collaborative, hands-on approach that treats execution as part of strategy, not a handoff after the recommendation.
• Helpful, but not required: experience with usage-based or consumption models, international expansion, enterprise or platform sales, or a technical or scientific background. Interest in people management over time is welcome, but this is an individual contributor role.
 About the team 
 The Revenue Strategy team tackles strategic questions about how GitLab reaches customers, sells, and monetizes its platform. You'll work with Sales, Finance, and Product leaders to connect strategy with commercial decisions, and with Field Operations and Enablement to put those decisions into practice. GitLab is an all-remote company with a public handbook and a transparent, low-ego culture. Our mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

title: Senior Product Manager, Trust & Safety, Integrity and Fraud
description:
Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 About the Team
 Our Trust & Safety, Integrity and Fraud Product team is dedicated to ensuring a safe and trusted experience for all customers across our platform, including Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers. We tackle complex challenges, from preventing fraud, abuse and Account Takeover to ensuring authenticity, to building regulatory compliance capabilities, all while balancing risk mitigation and providing a seamless user experience. Our team partners closely with cross-functional groups, including Engineering, Data Science, Compliance, and Risk Operations, to drive strategic initiatives that protect our business while fostering growth.
 About the Role
 Trust is foundational to an on-demand marketplace. Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt are converging European capabilities into one platform and one global product capability to prevent fraud and abuse. The marketplace is expanding rapidly beyond just restaurants as we become “your door to more." As we add new products, geographies, ways for Consumers, Merchants and Couriers to engage, we’re expanding and enhancing our fraud capabilities to be best in the industry at keeping our platform safe and trustworthy. We strongly believe that trust is the most important attribute of an online marketplace, and the team ensures that we maintain this trust.
 We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager that will lead dedicated cross-functional teams to solve complex challenges that impact Consumers, Couriers and Merchants and touch every corner of our business - from new user onboarding, to the in-app delivery experience, to the products and services being created that our users can’t find anywhere else. We are looking to hire for a few roles, so you’ll either lead a vertical fraud team protecting Consumers, Couriers or Merchants, or lead a horizontal fraud platform team focused on building our Risk Engine, Data Signals Intelligence and Automation / Anomaly Detection capabilities or leading compliance and authenticity efforts involving Identity Verification and Right to Work. The Fraud team is in hyper growth in terms of its size and impact and offers a unique opportunity to set and execute on a vision that will shape the future of Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt globally.
 You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
• Set the vision and long-term product strategy for one of our vertical fraud teams or our horizontal platform fraud team.
• Prevent, detect and mitigate fraud and abuse, building and leveraging AI systems to address risk in real time.
• Build an AI-led fraud operations platform that turns complex marketplace signals into automated decisions, prioritised investigations, and actionable case workflows, stopping fraud, abuse and manipulation before incidents occur.
• Develop and execute a customer-focused product roadmap through close collaboration with senior leadership, Operations, Data Science, Analytics, Design, and Engineering all while balancing business needs.
• Translate customer and internal-user needs into clear, well-defined functional and technical requirements backed by data analysis and deep understanding of our users
• Guide and interface closely with data analysis and engineering teams to define scope, review and refine technical capabilities, prioritize projects for release, and define new opportunities.
